# 9.43 A reduction in a fixed order
Part: a reduction in a fixed order gives the same bits on every run
Clause: CUDA C++ Programming Guide, Atomic Functions (atomicAdd: the order of the operations is not fixed); IEEE 754-2019 §10.4 (the order of operations fixes a floating-point result); [expr.add]
After: 9.01, 9.27
Levels: c++23
Device: yes
Source: CUDA C++ Programming Guide, Atomic Functions; Higham, Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms, 2nd ed., §4.1 and §4.2 (a sum's rounding errors depend on the order of its additions)

## Example
```cuda
#include <cstddef>
#include <cuda/std/span>
#include <print>
#include <vector>

__global__ void lane_sums(cuda::std::span<const float> x,
                          cuda::std::span<float> s)
{
    std::size_t lane {blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x};
    if (lane < s.size()) {
        float sum {0.0f};
        std::size_t step {s.size()};
        for (std::size_t i {lane}; i < x.size(); i += step) {
            sum = sum + x[i];
        }
        s[lane] = sum;
    }
}

float reduce(const std::vector<float>& h, std::size_t lanes,
             unsigned b)
{
    std::size_t n {h.size()};
    float* d {nullptr};
    cudaMalloc(&d, (n + lanes) * sizeof(float));
    cudaMemcpy(d, h.data(), n * sizeof(float),
               cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);
    unsigned blocks {static_cast<unsigned>(lanes / b + 1)};
    lane_sums<<<blocks, b>>>({d, n}, {d + n, lanes});
    std::vector<float> s(lanes, 0.0f);
    cudaMemcpy(s.data(), d + n, lanes * sizeof(float),
               cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);
    cudaFree(d);
    for (std::size_t half {lanes / 2}; half > 0; half /= 2) {
        for (std::size_t l {0}; l < half; ++l) {
            s[l] = s[l] + s[l + half];
        }
    }
    return s[0];
}

int main()
{
    //: Take 4096 floats 1000/(i mod 97 + 1) to sum.
    std::vector<float> h(4096, 0.0f);
    for (std::size_t i {0}; i < h.size(); ++i) {
        h[i] = 1000.0f / static_cast<float>(i % 97 + 1);
    }
    //: Fix the order by 1024 lanes, whatever the block size.
    float a {reduce(h, 1024, 64)};
    float b {reduce(h, 1024, 256)};
    std::println("fixed: {:a} {:a}", a, b);
    //: Tie the lanes to the block size, and the order moves.
    float c {reduce(h, 64, 64)};
    float e {reduce(h, 256, 256)};
    //: See the same bits twice, then two other sums.
    std::println("tied: {:a} {:a}", c, e);
}
```

## Verdict 1
```cuda
#include <cuda/std/span>
#include <print>

__global__ void add(cuda::std::span<const float> x, float* sum)
{
    atomicAdd(sum, x[threadIdx.x]);
}

int main()
{
    float* d {nullptr};
    cudaMallocManaged(&d, 4 * sizeof(float));
    d[0] = 0x1p24f;
    d[1] = 1.0f;
    d[2] = 1.0f;
    d[3] = 0.0f;
    add<<<1, 3>>>({d, 3}, d + 3);
    cudaDeviceSynchronize();
    std::println("{:a}", d[3]);
    cudaFree(d);
}
```
Answer: unspecified
```out
1p+24
```
```out
1.000002p+24
```

## Verdict 2
```cuda
#include <cuda/std/span>
#include <print>

__global__ void add(cuda::std::span<const float> x, float* sum)
{
    for (float v : x) {
        *sum = *sum + v;
    }
}

int main()
{
    float* d {nullptr};
    cudaMallocManaged(&d, 4 * sizeof(float));
    d[0] = 0x1p24f;
    d[1] = 1.0f;
    d[2] = 1.0f;
    d[3] = 0.0f;
    add<<<1, 1>>>({d, 3}, d + 3);
    cudaDeviceSynchronize();
    std::println("{:a}", d[3]);
    cudaFree(d);
}
```
Answer: defined

## Alone 1
Form: run
Write a program that sums n floats on the device in a fixed order, so that the bits printed are the same for every block size B. Use 1024 lanes, whatever B is, with one thread per lane in blocks of B threads. Lane l sums xₗ, xₗ₊₁₀₂₄, xₗ₊₂₀₄₈, … in float, in index order, from 0. Then add the 1024 lane sums sₗ by halving: for h = 512, 256, …, 1 in turn, set sₗ to sₗ + sₗ₊ₕ for every l < h. Print s₀.
Input: n and B on the first line, then x₀ … xₙ₋₁ on one line, read as floats.
Output: one line, the sum, as std::format prints it with {:a}.
Limits: 1 ≤ n ≤ 5000; B is 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 or 1024; each xᵢ is between −100 and 100 with at most three digits after the point.
### Examples
```in
3 1024
32.606 83.808 -52.064
```
```out
1.016666p+6
```
```in
4 1024
1 2 3 4
```
```out
1.4p+3
```
### Reference
```cuda
#include <cstddef>
#include <cuda/std/span>
#include <iostream>
#include <print>
#include <vector>

__global__ void lane_sums(cuda::std::span<const float> x,
                          cuda::std::span<float> s)
{
    std::size_t lane {blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x};
    if (lane < s.size()) {
        float sum {0.0f};
        std::size_t step {s.size()};
        for (std::size_t i {lane}; i < x.size(); i += step) {
            sum = sum + x[i];
        }
        s[lane] = sum;
    }
}

int main()
{
    std::size_t n {0};
    unsigned b {0};
    std::cin >> n >> b;
    std::vector<float> h(n, 0.0f);
    for (float& v : h) {
        std::cin >> v;
    }
    std::size_t lanes {1024};
    float* d {nullptr};
    cudaMalloc(&d, (n + lanes) * sizeof(float));
    cudaMemcpy(d, h.data(), n * sizeof(float),
               cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);
    unsigned blocks {static_cast<unsigned>(lanes / b + 1)};
    lane_sums<<<blocks, b>>>({d, n}, {d + n, lanes});
    std::vector<float> s(lanes, 0.0f);
    cudaMemcpy(s.data(), d + n, lanes * sizeof(float),
               cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);
    cudaFree(d);
    for (std::size_t half {lanes / 2}; half > 0; half /= 2) {
        for (std::size_t l {0}; l < half; ++l) {
            s[l] = s[l] + s[l + half];
        }
    }
    std::println("{:a}", s[0]);
}
```

## Alone 2
Form: run
Write a kernel that adds n floats into one total with atomicAdd, one thread each, and gives the same exact total on every run. Every xᵢ is a whole number, so turn each into a 64-bit integer and add those.
Input: n on the first line, then x₀ … xₙ₋₁ on one line, read as floats.
Output: one line, the exact total as a whole number.
Limits: 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000; each xᵢ is a whole number from −16777216 to 16777216, or −33554432, or 33554432.
### Examples
```in
3
1 2 3
```
```out
6
```
```in
2
-5 7
```
```out
2
```
### Reference
```cuda
#include <cstddef>
#include <cuda/std/span>
#include <iostream>
#include <print>
#include <vector>

using Acc = unsigned long long;

__global__ void total(cuda::std::span<const float> x,
                      cuda::std::span<Acc> sum)
{
    std::size_t i {blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x};
    if (i < x.size()) {
        long long v {static_cast<long long>(x[i])};
        atomicAdd(&sum[0], static_cast<Acc>(v));
    }
}

int main()
{

    for (float& v : h) {
        std::cin >> v;
    }
    float* d {nullptr};
    cudaMalloc(&d, n * sizeof(float));
    cudaMemcpy(d, h.data(), n * sizeof(float),
               cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);
    Acc* s {nullptr};
    cudaMalloc(&s, sizeof(Acc));
    cudaMemset(s, 0, sizeof(Acc));
    unsigned blocks {static_cast<unsigned>(n / 128 + 1)};
    total<<<blocks, 128>>>({d, n}, {s, 1});
    Acc bits {0};
    cudaMemcpy(&bits, s, sizeof(bits), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);
    cudaFree(s);
    cudaFree(d);
    std::println("{}", static_cast<long long>(bits));
}
```
